answer: Resisting sybils means designing for scarcity, not for trust. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a trellis the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single dawn of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a karst of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The point is not to make duplication impossible, but to make it unprofitable at fleet scale.
